name: TileLang-TPU
summary: A TileLang backend for SOPHGO TPUs, from compile-time memory planning to executable kernels.
overview: TileLang-TPU brings tile-level programming to commercial SOPHGO accelerators. Tiles are small blocks of data used to express a computation. The compiler handles on-chip memory placement, data movement and overlapping transfers with computation. Its just-in-time (JIT) runtime compiles Python kernel definitions and launches them on the BM1690.

highlights.title: Static memory allocation
highlights.description: Plan where each data block sits in the chip’s fast local memory before the program runs, following the hardware’s placement rules and staying within its capacity.

highlights.title: Overlap transfers and computation
highlights.description: Arrange data transfers and computation into stages that can run in parallel, with each step starting only when its required data is ready.

highlights.title: Generate and run TPU code
highlights.description: Translate the computation into operations the TPU can execute, then compile, load and launch the program.

evaluation.baseline: Vendor PPL implementations used by SOPHGO Torch-TPU
evaluation.metric: PPL operator execution time / TileLang-TPU operator execution time

standalone.aggregation: Average speedup by operator category across tested configurations and data types

flash_attention.optimization: Head-batched computation: process multiple attention heads together

source.type: owner-supplied updated evaluation summary and figures

evaluation.scope: Evaluated on a single core of the SOPHGO BM1690, with input sizes fixed before compilation. The baseline is the vendor’s optimized PPL implementation used by Torch-TPU. PPL (Primitive Programming Language) is SOPHGO’s low-level programming language.
evaluation.methods: Speedup compares execution time for the tested operations. Standalone results report averages by operator category. FlashAttention and fused MLP are separate workloads, each with its own average.
evaluation.standalone_text: We evaluated matrix multiplication, RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU and element-wise addition across multiple input configurations and numerical formats. RMSNorm rescales values, RoPE encodes sequence positions and SwiGLU applies a nonlinear neural-network transformation. Average speedups by operator category are 1.05–1.23× over PPL.
evaluation.attention_text: TileLang-TPU also supports fused operators that combine multiple computation steps. FlashAttention efficiently computes model attention. After an algorithm optimization that processes multiple attention heads together in a batch (head-batched), it achieves an average speedup of 12.50× over PPL. Attention heads are parallel computation branches that attend to different information.
evaluation.mlp_text: For a fused MLP, a feed-forward neural network commonly used within AI models, the MLP W8A16 Dequantized Forward operator averages 1.01× over PPL, essentially matching its performance. W8A16 uses 8-bit weights and 16-bit activations. Dequantization converts the stored low-precision weights into values used by the computation.

figures.alt: Speedup of five operator categories over PPL across five input configurations and three floating-point formats.
figures.caption: Standalone operators. M0–M4 label five tested input configurations. BF16 and FP16 use 16-bit floating-point formats; FP32 uses 32 bits. A value of 1× means the same execution time as PPL, and larger values mean faster execution. The 1.05–1.23× summary gives averages by operator category.

figures.alt: FlashAttention average speedup of 12.50 times and fused MLP average speedup of 1.01 times over PPL.
figures.caption: Fused workloads. FlashAttention averages 12.50× over PPL; the W8A16 MLP averages 1.01×. B, H, S and D denote batch size, attention heads, sequence length and head dimension. M, H and I denote input rows, hidden width and intermediate width. The tuples identify the tested input sizes.
